title: Kafka Streams Basics
description: Build stateful stream processing topologies with the Kafka Streams library.

data.text: **Kafka Streams** is a lightweight Java library for building real-time stream processing applications that run on top of Apache Kafka. Unlike full cluster frameworks such as Apache Flink or Spark Streaming, Kafka Streams runs as a library inside your own application, giving you full control over deployment, scaling, and monitoring while handling partitions, state stores, and fault tolerance automatically.

Kafka Streams models processing logic as a directed graph of **stream processors** connected by **streams**. The top-level abstractions are `KStream` (a record stream) and `KTable` (a changelog stream representing the latest value for each key). A `KStream` can be transformed with stateless operations such as `map` and `filter`, or stateful operations such as `groupByKey` and `aggregate`.

terms.definition: An immutable record stream where each record represents a self-contained data item.
A changelog stream that represents the latest value for each key, effectively a table view over a stream.
The directed acyclic graph of stream processors that defines how data flows through your application.
A persistent, fault-tolerant store used by stateful operators such as aggregations and joins.

data.text: A typical Kafka Streams application reads from one or more input topics, applies transformations, and writes results to output topics. The library handles consumer group coordination, partition assignment, and state store recovery automatically. When a node fails, its partitions and state stores are migrated to another instance without downtime.

data.title: Java Kafka Streams Word Count
data.content: A minimal Kafka Streams topology that counts words in real time using the High-Level DSL.

data.text: Kafka Streams supports **exactly-once processing semantics (EOS)** when both the input and output topics are compacted and the application is configured with `processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2`. Under EOS, every record is processed exactly once, even in the presence of failures, by using transactional writes and read-process-write loops coordinated by Kafka's transaction API.

data.title: Interactive Queries
data.text: Kafka Streams exposes state stores via Interactive Queries, allowing external applications to read the latest aggregation results directly from a running stream application without querying the output topic.

items.question: Is Kafka Streams only for Java applications?
items.answer: Kafka Streams is a Java library, but it can be used from any JVM language such as Kotlin or Scala. For .NET and Node.js, consider ksqlDB or Kafka Connect for integration.

items.question: How does Kafka Streams handle large state?
items.answer: State is stored in local RocksDB instances backed by changelog topics in Kafka. If state grows beyond a single machine, you can scale by increasing the number of application instances.

items.question: What is the difference between DSL and Processor API?
items.answer: The DSL is a high-level, declarative API for common operations. The Processor API gives you fine-grained control over record routing, scheduling, and punctuation for advanced use cases.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Kafka Streams runs as a library inside your JVM application
KStream models a record stream; KTable models a changelog view
State stores persist aggregation and join state locally with changelog topics
Exactly-once processing requires transactional producer configuration
data.takeaway: Kafka Streams brings stream processing directly into your application with automatic scaling and fault tolerance.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Kafka Streams App
data.description: Create a Kafka Streams application that processes a stream of click events and counts clicks per URL in 1-minute tumbling windows.
steps: Create a new Maven or Gradle project with the Kafka Streams dependency
Define a Serde for the click event key (URL) and value
Build a topology using the DSL with groupBy, windowedBy, and count
Materialize the count into a state store and write to an output topic
Run the application and produce test click events with kafka-console-producer
data.expectedOutcome: A running Kafka Streams app that emits per-URL click counts every minute
